question: does the Lean qPochhammer in habiro-precision-ladder-equivalence match the expansion it formalizes?
answer: No. It used prod(1-u^{2k}) = (u^2;u^2)_m where the corpus's stored Habiro coefficients are computed against (u;u)_m = prod(1-u^k) at u = sqrt(q). Reconstructing tr_M with the Lean's convention gives 6.9602 instead of 1.1458 (507 %). Corrected in the Lean and the .md.
scope: (b) for the discrepancy — an exact arithmetic mismatch against a stored witness, with the convention declared by the witness itself. (a) for the fix direction. Confined to the FORMALIZATION: the compute layer already used (1-u^k), so no published number was wrong, and the corrected declaration has zero external consumers.
lean_verification: lean -DautoImplicit=false -s 65536 -> exit 0, 0 errors (never lake build; restored olean cache intact)
separate_defect_reported_not_fixed: computations/habiro/habiro_exact_qbeta.py::eval_a_m_at_u does u = float(u_val) — float64 — contradicting a comment 25 lines below in the same file; it emits habiro-exact-qbeta.witness.json.

assertions.name: witness_declares_the_1_minus_u_k_convention
assertions.detail: habiro-coefficients-atomic.witness.json description: 'Habiro / cyclotomic expansion tr_M(T_w, q) = Σ_m a_m·(check_q;check_q)_m (check_q = q^{1/2}) for atomic braids p, n (def' — i.e. the expansion is against (check_q;check_q)_m with check_q = q^{1/2}, which is prod(1-u^k) at u = sqrt(q). The convention is stated by the data itself, not inferred.

assertions.name: 1_minus_u_k_reproduces_the_stored_trM
assertions.detail: p (proton, A=1): 4.648e-17; n (neutron, A=1): 4.116e-17 — both atoms reconstruct to better than 1e-15 at 60 dps, evaluating the a_m through sympy exact rationals rather than the producer's float64 path.

assertions.name: 1_minus_u_2k_is_off_by_hundreds_of_percent
assertions.detail: p (proton, A=1): rel 5.075 (6.960179408595493079945 vs 1.145759692457300816435); n (neutron, A=1): rel 3.622 (4.564900350080829571584 vs 0.987743688115809530983) — this is what the Lean definition and the .md both specified. Not a rounding question: 507 % and 362 %.

assertions.name: it_was_also_a_notation_error_independently
assertions.detail: (u;u)_m DENOTES prod(1-u^k); prod(1-u^{2k}) is (u^2;u^2)_m. So the definition disagreed with the name it was given whichever expansion one wants — the same name-vs-body class as markovZ / markovZC / markovZc (#5972, #6015). Two of the three QOU.BraidKnot.qPochhammer definitions in mass-theory/ (habiro-expansion-atomic, full-pole-structure-mass-trace) already used (1-u^k); the equivalence file was the only one that did not.
